per_scope.contains: per blocker: the guarded days, each day's file/manifest/roster with their sha256, requested-outcome accounting, the residual confirmed-trading-gap list (present even when empty), and the scope's own all_checks_passed
per_scope.why_per_scope: a single shared file written per scope would let a B2 run overwrite the B1 attestation. The per-scope files are the durable records; they are never rewritten by another scope's run.
per_scope.written_by: one --stage verify run, for its own scope only

admission_evidence.trust_rule: the consumer re-hashes every referenced file itself; this evidence is a pointer, not an authority

union.cli_exit_semantics: --stage verify exits 0 when every day THIS run was asked about passed its checks (days_verified_ok), which is the honest outcome for a --days subset. Scope-wide readiness is reported separately as all_scopes_ready in the printed output and must not be inferred from the exit code.
union.contains: scopes{<scope>: {state, reason, is_full_scope, required_days, required_day_count, admitted_days, verified_subset_days, missing_required_days, unadmitted_days, residual_confirmed_trading_gaps, source, source_sha256, verified_at, requested_outcome_accounting, failed_checks, rehash{days_rehashed, mismatches}}}, blockers{<B1,B2>: {scope, state, is_full_scope, required_day_count, admitted_day_count, missing_required_day_count, admitted_days, verified_subset_days, unadmitted_days, residual_confirmed_trading_gaps}}, readiness_rule, missing_scopes, stale_scopes, all_scopes_ready, days_verified_ok, verified_scope, verified_days, is_subset_run
union.day_admission_rule: a day is admitted only when its own verify checks all pass. status=complete alone is never sufficient: a stale manifest claiming complete while its checks fail lands the day in unadmitted_days with verify_checks_failed populated.
union.no_fabricated_pass: a scope with no attestation is reported in missing_scopes with state=unverified and an empty admitted_days. all_scopes_ready is false whenever any scope is missing, stale, a verified_subset or not ready. The union never invents evidence for a scope it does not have, and never treats a subset as a discharge of the whole.
union.readiness_rule: A scope is ready ONLY when its admitted day set equals every guarded dev day the scope owes: B1 = 19 days of 2025-02, B2 = 41 days of 2026-04/05. The counts are derived from the dev calendar via full_scope_day_set(), never hardcoded, so a calendar change cannot leave readiness asserting a stale total. Admitting one verified day of nineteen does not discharge the blocker.
union.rehash_rule: the union re-hashes every admitted day's parquet and manifest at publish time. A day that no longer hashes to what its attestation recorded is named in rehash.mismatches and dropped, so a manifest that still claims status=complete cannot keep a corrupted payload admitted.
scope_states: ready - parents match, the scope's own all_checks_passed is true, every required day was admitted, and every one of them re-hashed correctly just now

verified_subset - the scope's own checks passed for the days it ran, but it covered fewer than every required day. admitted_days is EMPTY; the days it did verify are listed under verified_subset_days, and every uncovered day is named in missing_required_days. This state can never be read as full coverage
not_ready - the file exists and the parents match, but the scope's own checks failed or a day no longer hashes; admitted_days is emptied
stale - produced by a different acquisition root, code, contract, PIT or alias-map identity; it contributes nothing
unverified - no per-scope attestation has been produced for that scope at all
union.written_by: every --stage verify run, REBUILT from the per-scope files on disk (never appended to)

admission_states.admitted: status=complete, no errors, no unresolved contradictory zeros: the day replaces/augments the baseline raw lane
admission_states.incomplete: an error occurred, or a compact-observed symbol came back with zero bars, or the payload is empty: the day is NOT admitted and is listed in the residual confirmed-trading gaps
admission_states.note: there is no 'partial' admission and no ack flag; a day is either complete or it is not admitted

alias_rule.allowed_basis: class_share_separator: the PIT archive spells a share class with '/' and the provider's own data uses '.'; the mapping is a separator transliteration of the SAME name, backed by the provider's own spelling appearing in a same-provider lane artifact
forbidden_basis: price similarity or volume similarity of any kind
bare-stripping of a '^' unit suffix (MS^A is NOT MSA; a stripped base that happens to be a different listed company is a different instrument)
any inference from 'the name looks like it should be X'
alias_rule.injective: one canonical name maps to at most one provider spelling AND one provider spelling maps to at most one canonical name; a collision is a hard error that refuses the day, because two identities may never share one payload
alias_rule.no_dedup_by_price: two canonical names with identical price series stay two names. Aliases are spelling, never economics.
alias_rule.unresolved_syntax_names: a syntax PIT name with no verified provider spelling is recorded in the roster's no_verified_provider_spelling class. It is never requested under a guessed spelling.

B1_raw_2025_02.request_rule: every canonical PIT name of the day; the same-day acquisition file REPLACES the fallback for those days

B2_raw_roster_2026_04_05.baseline_lane: data/backfill/ohlcv_<month>.parquet (raw SIP backfill, partial PIT coverage)
B2_raw_roster_2026_04_05.request_rule: only evidence-backed missing names: PIT x compact-universe-present minus names the baseline lane already carries in-window for that day, plus the syntax names with a VERIFIED provider spelling

flags: --days comma-separated guarded dev days (optional; default the whole scope)
cli.secrets: ALPACA_API_KEY/ALPACA_SECRET_KEY from the environment or the repo .env; never written to any artifact or log
cli.stages: plan (offline, writes the acquisition plan), acquire (network), verify (offline, writes the admission evidence)

coverage_standing.aprmay2026: the acquired day file SUPPLEMENTS the baseline raw lane, so a compact-observed name is covered when it is in the payload OR already in the baseline lane in-window for that day
coverage_standing.feb2025: the acquired day file REPLACES the floored clean fallback, so every compact-observed PIT name must be present in that payload alone
coverage_standing.uncovered: anything still uncovered is an unresolved missing confirmed trader. It is listed in the roster's accounting and in the admission evidence, never assumed away.

data_roots.market_data: outside the worktree, read-only, gitignored (BASKET_DATA_ROOT, ROOT/data, /home/hillel/projects/Alpacatrader/data)
data_roots.tracked_evidence: factory/artifacts/basket/phase2/ATLAS/TAPE/OBSERVATION/v0 (this contract, the alias map and admission hashes/counts only; never market rows)

error_semantics.api_error: 429/5xx/transport are retried with bounded backoff; on exhaustion the error is recorded and the day is incomplete and unadmitted.
error_semantics.contradictory_zero: ANY source that recorded a positive bar count for a name - the compact SIP source OR the baseline lane - is the oracle. Keying it on the compact source alone was structurally blind to names that source never observed, which is how baseline-only names were recorded as clean provider zeros. Recorded with the observed count, left UNRESOLVED, and it blocks admission.
error_semantics.duplicate_rows: a repeated (ticker,timestamp) is a payload integrity error; the day is incomplete.
error_semantics.invalid_symbol: the provider rejects the spelling. Recorded in symbols_invalid with the reason, never renamed to something that might work.
error_semantics.out_of_window: a bar outside the declared window is a payload integrity error; the day is incomplete.
error_semantics.request_failed: A symbol we never completed a request for is recorded in symbols_request_failed, never as a zero. The three symbol classes are disjoint and mean different things: symbols_invalid (the provider rejected the spelling), symbols_request_failed (we know nothing about whether it traded), symbols_zero_bars (a genuine provider zero). Any request_failed symbol blocks admission with refusal_reasons containing request_failed_symbols.
error_semantics.symbols_zero_bars: the provider accepted the spelling and returned no bar. Recorded in symbols_zero_bars; a legitimate zero is recorded, never fabricated.

estimator.bytes: rows x 96 planning bytes/row; the real size is always read back from the written file
estimator.measured_not_estimated: every run reports measured bytes and measured rows per day in the manifest
estimator.requests: ceil(requested_symbols / 500) batches, one paginated request stream per batch
estimator.rows: per-symbol bar count from the compact SIP source; bars_per_day_reference for names the compact source does not carry

evidence_rule: a name is repairable only when some source shows it actually printed that session. The compact SIP source (data/sip/universe/rth/<day>.parquet) is that evidence. absent_all_sources names are never requested: a name that did not trade is not a hole, and asking the provider cannot manufacture a print.

fetch.asof_rule: Every request carries an explicit historical asof=YYYY-MM-DD equal to the session day, in BOTH the SDK (StockBarsRequest(asof=...)) and the REST client (params['asof']). Without it the provider applies default entity linking and can attribute a renamed entity's tape to the queried PIT name, which is a PIT-identity violation. asof is part of the config hash, so a run cannot silently resume days fetched without it.
fetch.paging: next_page_token followed to exhaustion by the REST client; the SDK client is called without a limit so the SDK pages internally. A repeated page_token is an error, not a loop.
fetch.retry: bounded: 429/5xx/transport retried with exponential backoff (2,4,8,16s, capped 30s) honouring Retry-After up to 60s; on exhaustion the error is recorded and the day is incomplete. Unbounded retrying is refused.
fetch.universe_rule: the PIT archive (data/pit/pit_symbols.parquet, latest vintage <= day) plus per-day compact-universe evidence. A 'latest active assets' list is NEVER fetched: present-day listings are not a point-in-time roster.
fetch.upper_bound_meaning: A bar stamped 16:05 ET is a vendor bar timestamp at the window's upper bound. Nothing in the acquisition or the frozen contracts identifies it as an auction, a close, or any particular session event, so it is described only by its timestamp. The baseline backfill lane already carries 412 bars stamped 16:05 for 2026-04-01, so the acquired day agrees with the lane it supplements.
fetch.window_bounds_rule: CLOSED interval [565, 965] on both ends. A bar stamped exactly at 16:05 ET is IN window and is kept. This matches the frozen observation contract's declared closed projection window "[565, 965] (09:25-16:05 ET)", the consumer's grid range(565, 966), and the provider's inclusive end parameter. The request end is the bound itself with no epsilon subtracted.

guard.calendar: basket_sim.dev_days() (date stems of factory/artifacts/basket/sip/anatomy/*.jsonl); a day in the scope that is not a dev day is not acquirable
guard.refusal: a sealed or reserved day, or a --days value outside the scope's guarded set, raises before any file is opened. There is no flag that admits a sealed day.
guard.source: factory/scripts/basket_sim.py:guard_day (called via dev_days()/directly before any path is opened)

obligation.aprmay2026: the acquired day file SUPPLEMENTS the baseline lane, which stays in place, so the obligation is PIT x compact-observed and the lane covers its own names.
obligation.evidence_rule: every obligated name must carry a positive bar count from some source; an obligation without evidence would be unfalsifiable.
obligation.feb2025: the acquired day file REPLACES the floored fallback, so the obligation is PIT x (compact-observed UNION replaced-baseline in-window). A PIT name the fallback carried but the compact source never observed is STILL owed; keying the obligation on compact alone silently dropped BK and ARMN on 19 of 19 days with status=complete.

payload.atomicity: each day is written to <name>.tmp then os.replace'd, bars first then the manifest; the manifest carries the payload sha256

root_layout.evidence/acquisition_admission.json: B1/B2 admission evidence for the consumer gate
root_layout.rosters/<day>.json: per-day PIT roster, provider mapping, verified-absent classes

payload.row_policy: every bar the provider returns for a requested symbol is written, including non-positive or inconsistent OHLC. Quality is graded downstream by the consumer's flag_nonpositive_px machinery; acquisition never drops a row to make itself look clean.

schema.provider_symbol: String (audit only; never a join key)
schema.ticker: String (CANONICAL PIT spelling; the only join key)

purpose: Freeze HOW the two missing raw SIP lanes (B1 2025-02, B2 2026-04/05) are reacquired, so the observation corpus can claim an unfiltered raw source for every guarded day. This contract governs acquisition only: it declares no representation, no distance, no channel, no learned parameter and no outcome. Nothing here decides what the acquired tape is later used for.

resource_policy.digest_cache: content hashes are memoized per process on (size, mtime_ns), so the 585 MiB lane is hashed once per run rather than once per day (~25 GiB of re-reads removed). A modified file is always rehashed.
resource_policy.interning: lane tickers are interned; ~212k references collapse to ~10.8k distinct string objects.
resource_policy.lane_read: per-day predicate-pushed streaming projection; the month-wide group_by/agg form materialised a hash table over all ~10.8M tickers of a 585 MiB file and peaked at +1740 MiB per month, running twice and retaining both dicts. Measured after the fix: 0.0 MiB peak growth over 8 B2 planning days, and faster.
resource_policy.no_truncation: these are streaming and caching changes only. No ROI, density or row-count truncation is applied anywhere; every bar returned is written.
resource_policy.pit_read: vintages are indexed by name only; a vintage's symbols are read on demand instead of materializing all 1397 vintages (~8.1M strings, a measured 127 MiB).

resume_and_drift.drift_checked_first: the code/config/contract hash comparison runs BEFORE the resume skip, so an intact admitted day is still refused when the current run has a different window, batch, client, scope, contract or producer. That day was acquired under a different configuration, and keeping the old bytes would silently hide it.
resume_and_drift.drift_scope: the config hash covers feed, adjustment, timeframe, window, batch size, retry attempts, scope and client, so a rerun under any changed acquisition setting must target a new version directory
resume_and_drift.never_overwrite: admitted bytes are never rewritten. A payload whose bytes disagree with its manifest, a torn write (payload without manifest), or a code/config/contract hash that differs from the stored one STOP the run and ask for a new version directory (--out-data .../acquisition/vN).
resume_and_drift.resume: an existing day whose manifest is status=complete and whose payload still hashes to the recorded sha is skipped, never refetched
resume_and_drift.versioning: acquisition/v0 is the admitted version; a schema, window, batch or contract change requires v1 rather than a silent rewrite of v0

covers: payload schema, dtypes and ordering; the synthetic bars are built on the ET clock so the window check is exercised honestly
duplicate (ticker,timestamp) detected
out-of-window row detected
paginated pages are joined into one symbol's bar list
truncated page stream yields a recorded zero, never a fabricated bar
invalid symbol is recorded and the batch continues with the rest
REST next_page_token paging followed to exhaustion; a repeated token is refused rather than looped
429 retried with bounded backoff, then surfaced once the bound is exhausted
sealed, reserved and malformed days refused before any path is opened; an out-of-scope --days value is refused
the same provider spelling under two canonical names is refused in the payload and in the alias map
an alias map entry without explicit spelling evidence is refused
sha resume skips an intact admitted day; tampered admitted bytes, torn writes and empty payloads are refused
code, config and contract hash drift on an existing day stops the run and asks for a new version
a zero-bar symbol is recorded rather than fabricated, and a compact-observed name that contradicts it blocks admission with the contradiction stated explicitly
verify flags uncovered compact-observed symbols, an incomplete status, an unresolved contradiction, producer drift and a manifest window that disagrees with the contract
a fully covered day with no contradiction IS admitted, with one row set per canonical name
coverage standing differs correctly by scope: feb2025 requires the payload alone, aprmay2026 credits the baseline lane
admitted_days contains only days whose own verify checks all passed; an incomplete or check-failing day is listed in unadmitted_days with its reasons and its failed check names
the union publisher: verifying B1 then B2 retains BOTH scope entries and both blocker ids, so a B2 run can never overwrite the B1 attestation
a scope with no attestation stays in missing_scopes with state=unverified and an empty admitted_days; the union never fabricates a pass
corrupting an admitted day payload invalidates the union at publish time even though its manifest still says status=complete, because the union re-hashes every included day
a corrupted scope leaves the other scope's entry intact
an attestation produced by a different root/code/contract/PIT/alias identity is marked stale and contributes nothing
a scope whose own checks failed contributes no admitted days

a one-day --days subset per scope cannot resolve a full scope: both scopes report verified_subset with EMPTY admitted_days, list the days they did verify under verified_subset_days, and name every missing required day
a full-scope attestation covering all 19 B1 and all 41 B2 days IS ready, and the blocker entries report the matching admitted_day_count
a baseline-only name (in the replaced fallback, absent from compact) is obligated, and a fresh zero for it is a contradiction that blocks admission - the BK/ARMN case
a symbol whose request never completed is recorded as request_failed, never as a zero, and blocks admission
selftests.isolation: synthetic and offline: scripted fetchers and fake HTTP sessions only, temporary directories only, no network and no shared data root

verify_checks: guarded exact target days: the verified day set equals the scope's guarded dev days (or the --days filter), and every day passed guard_day
manifest day equals the filename date, scope matches, source feed is sip and adjustment is raw
payload sha256 equals the manifest sha256; roster sha256 and code sha256 match the current producer
schema is exactly the eight declared columns with the declared dtypes (timestamp is ns UTC)
all OHLC finite and positive with high >= max(open,close) >= min(open,close) >= low
every row timestamp falls inside the declared 09:25-16:05 ET window
all requested symbols accounted for: present, or in symbols_zero_bars, or in symbols_invalid
no unrequested symbol appears in the payload

all expected observed compact symbols are covered (see coverage_standing for what covered means per scope); a compact-observed symbol with zero fresh bars is an unresolved contradictory zero and blocks admission

versions.v0: first real fetch. Its manifest records status=incomplete: the window's upper bound was treated as exclusive, flagging 10 legitimate 16:05-stamped bars. Retained as evidence.
versions.v1: two ONE-DAY canaries. Not admissible: a subset never discharges a full scope.
versions.v2: 11 days fetched (4 B1 + 7 B2) before the audit. Retained immutable and UNADMITTED, and NOT trustworthy admitted evidence: baseline-only names were lost and asof was omitted.
versions.v3: the corrected root. Uses explicit historical asof and the full B1 obligation.
